title: Minimax Regret for Subsidy Allocation with Downside Semideviation Welfare in a Roy Model
banked_reason: The promised sharp, explicit common regret rate and attaining selector remain open; the delivered theorem is only a logarithmically unmatched bracket, so the proposed Stat frontier object is not yet supplied.
gap_reasons: The promised sharp, explicit common regret rate and attaining selector remain open; the delivered theorem is only a logarithmically unmatched bracket, so the proposed Stat frontier object is not yet supplied.

The delivered theorem establishes a same-class polynomial-order regret bracket, leaving upper-to-lower logarithmic factors of log(en)^(1-alpha) for d>beta and log(en)^(7/6) at d=beta=1; it does not determine the requested sharp rate.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived a total endpoint/Haar selector and an original-record randomized-selector converse, then enlarged the maintained class to conditional mean exclusion. The math referee passed the unmatched bracket, but the requested sharp logarithmic rate and critical corner remained an open question; an independent validity consult confirmed terminal kernel substitution. No formalization stage ran.
tldr: A half-budget subsidy planner evaluates mean conditional earnings minus their quadratic lower semideviation. On the smooth bounded benchmark with known product-uniform covariates, full-support continuous propensity and conditional mean exclusion, the contribution is an original-record \(p=2\) finite-sample expected-regret bracket for choosing between two deterministic feasible allocations. With \(\alpha=\beta/(2\beta+d)\) and \(L_n=\log(en)\), the lower order is \(n^{-\alpha}L_n^{\alpha-1}\); a total endpoint/Haar selector has upper order \(n^{-\alpha}\) when \(d>\beta\) and \(n^{-1/3}L_n^{1/2}\) when \(d=\beta=1\). The bounds apply on the same entire mean-exclusion class and permit exact ties, atoms at the welfare mean and vanishing downside risk. Propensity-independent Bernoulli laws serve as lower-bound witnesses inside that class. The exact logarithmic frontier and a sharp centered functional correction remain open.
gap: The direct allocation anchor supplies the welfare surface in its regret analysis and omits feasible first-stage error \cite{BurghMelo2026}. Endpoint recovery and zero semideviation interact in the maintained class. Its conditional mean exclusion does not fix the conditional outcome distributions required for the original marked-likelihood comparison; the supplied benchmark deliberately maintains conditional distributional exclusion.
fill: The kernel determines the sharp finite-sample regret order, constructs its original-record selector, and proves an all-selector converse without a minimum downside-risk or policy-gap condition.
